key_insight: The paper proposes a smooth, explicit elastoplastic-damage material update that uses closed-form branches, history projection, and exponential degradation to preserve irreversible deformation and damage without a local Newton solve.
engineering_relevance: This is useful for graphics and simulation pipelines that need stable, vectorizable material behavior for cyclic loading, unloading, and progressive failure with simple implementation.
method: Softplus generates a candidate equivalent plastic strain.
A max-history projection enforces irreversibility and a deviatoric plastic-strain tensor stores residual direction.
Damage evolves through an exponential scalar law driven by stored history, with active/frozen branches evaluated analytically from one response energy.
evidence_signal: The method is validated on 1D cyclic tension, 2D cantilever bending, 3D platen compression, and a genus-one torus, showing residual deformation, monotone internal variables, and branchwise energy-gradient agreement.
watch_item: It is intended for isotropic, proportional or nearly proportional loading; performance and accuracy drop sharply under large non-proportional path changes, and it is not a substitute for general return mapping or anisotropic damage models.
paper_title: A Smooth Explicit Elastoplastic--Damage Update for Graphics Simulation
